mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.2% in the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with weakening inflationary pressures, which increases risk aversion and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% monthly) and a rise in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a robust demand environment, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.4% AND HOUST rises > 2% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in unemployment rate to below 4% for three consecutive months, combined with accelerating wage growth (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly), signals a tight labor market and upward pressure on costs, which leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher corporate pricing power.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 3 consecutive months AND PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters indicates a weak macroeconomic backdrop, which depresses corporate earnings and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of quarters where GDPC1 < 1% for four consecutive quarters.
